criteria.description: 95% bootstrap CI lower bound on holdout AUC > 0.6
Brier skill score against the constant base-rate forecast > 0.05
top-decile hit rate at least 2x the base rate
mean absolute calibration error across deciles <= 0.05

bar.statement: All four criteria must pass. Accuracy at a 0.5 threshold is reported but is deliberately not a criterion: at an 8% base rate, always predicting "not a hit" already scores about 92%, so accuracy cannot separate a useful model from a useless one.

bandCoverage.note: Measured for #198. The band is a nominal 80% interval on the model's estimate of a film's hit probability, not a prediction interval for one film's binary outcome, so every test here is a group test. Which group makes the test valid is the whole question.

servingHorizonBand.note: The band a user sees is the one at the serving horizon, not the one a 2010 holdout film got. `meanWidthWithFlatTau` is what the band would be if drift stayed the single in-sample scalar it was before #198.

localNeighbourhood.method: For each film: the observed hit rate among films in the same roster-size stratum whose predicted probability is within 2 points, compared against that film's own band. This is the metric #198 cites.
localNeighbourhood.ceilingNote: A neighbourhood with no hits has an observed rate of exactly 0. The band's lower bound is a probability and is never 0, so those films cannot be covered by any band, however wide. `ceiling` is the share of films whose neighbourhood contains at least one hit — the largest coverage this metric can report on this data.

binned.method: Equal-count bins by predicted probability. `coverage` = share of bins whose observed rate is inside the mean band of its films; `coverageAllowingObservedCi` = share where the observed rate's 95% Wilson interval overlaps the band.

horizonDrift.method: Rolling origin inside 1965-2009: for each origin year the two Platt constants are fitted on the 8 years ending there, then the level offset that would have been needed is measured at each later training year. The holdout plays no part.

fit.form: driftSd(h) = base + perYear * h, h = max(0, anchorYear - fittedThrough)

commonMode.method: Per holdout year, the log-odds intercept shift that would have made that year calibrated. `sdOffset` is the quantity the band carries as tau; `rmsOffset` adds the level error the band does not carry. Measured on the holdout as a check — tau itself is fitted on the validation years and the holdout never sets it.

attribution.note: Holdout AUC when only the listed signals are allowed. Each row is refitted on the training period; the roster rows all use weight 1 per role.
attribution.note2: directorOnlyAuc here keeps only the director role, which answers #112. The D41-5 gate in backtest.ratingDeviationTerm.directorOnlyGate is a different comparison: it keeps every role's hit-rate effect and varies only which roles carry the rating term.

ratingDeviationTerm.form: Z = logit(genre base rate) + (1 - sharedCreditShare) * sum_r (roleWeight_r * effect_r + ratingDevWeight_r * ratingDev_r)
ratingDeviationTerm.fitForm: Penalty-free IRLS logistic regression of the outcome on the ten per-role pooled rating deviations, with the v1 score carried as a FREE-SLOPE covariate and a free intercept. Coefficients are divided by that slope to put them in engine units. A slope pinned to 1 is the wrong specification here and does not describe this run: see #224 and the correction note in docs/analytics/team-predictor-methodology.md section 2.
ratingDeviationTerm.fitV1ScoreSlopeNote: The slope of the v1 score in the FINAL pass (the survivors-only refit). The ten-role pass has its own, under tenRolePass.
ratingDeviationTerm.perRoleFitNote: One row per role. `pass` says which fit the row came from: "ten-role" for a role zeroed by rule 2, "survivors" for one that was refitted without the zeroed roles. The selection decision does not depend on the pass; `tenRolePass` holds the first pass in full so that can be checked.

tenRolePass.note: The first pass, before rule 2 zeroed anything: all ten rating deviations in one fit. Published because `perRoleFit` mixes this pass with the survivors-only refit (#224 ask 3).

directorOnlyGate.rule: D41-5, declared in docs/analytics/team-predictor-methodology.md before the holdout was scored: ship the per-role version unless the paired holdout difference against the director-only version has a 95% CI upper bound below zero.

leakagePlacebo.note: Rating-deviation features rebuilt from year + 1, so the film being predicted enters its own roster records. A leak must show up as a large AUC gain; the harness throws if it does not.

bandComparison.note: Shipped model against a v1 pipeline fitted on the same data in the same run. logOddsSd is what confidence is graded on; intervalWidth is in percentage points.

selection.rule: Rolling origin on 1990-2009: for each year, the two Platt constants are fitted on films released before it within the candidate window and scored on it. Selection is by pooled out-of-fold log loss among candidates whose shipped fitting window holds at least 1000 films. The holdout is not involved.
selection.note: Differences in pooled log loss between the 8, 10, 12 and 15-year windows are in the fourth decimal and should not be read as a ranking. What the table supports is "shorter than the whole training period": the level gap falls monotonically as the window shortens, which is the falling base rate being tracked.

aucInvariance.note: Recalibration is monotone, so it cannot change the ranking and cannot change AUC (F1-16). The residual is not exactly zero because hitProbability is rounded to four decimal places before scoring, which changes which films tie.

targets.note: #114's own definition of done, measured either way.

isotonicNotAttempted.item: #114 item 4 — isotonic or spline recalibration in place of the two-parameter logistic
isotonicNotAttempted.reason: The sprint doc's stated reason — that the top-end rigidity had largely gone away, worst decile 0.142 -> 0.049 — does not hold for this model: R1 alone takes the worst decile to 0.180, and the two-parameter recalibration brings it to 0.0525, which still misses #114's 0.05 target. The reason it is still not attempted is sample size, not the premise: a free-form monotone fit has to be estimated on the training period, where the top decile holds about 100 hits, and its top-end step would then be an extrapolation into a holdout whose base rate is 4 points lower. Two constants with a measured window are the defensible instrument at this sample size. The residual 0.0025 of target is one decile of 256 films and 77 hits.
